items.explanation: The source supports both positive assertions as scoped: the respondents are narrated as owners of the building at 41 Purani Mandi, and the trial court found that the appellant had sublet portions of the premises without written landlord consent. The property binding is also supported because the later discussion expressly describes the sublet property as 'some of the rooms of the building', so o7 is a direct proper part of o4. This does not extend the subletting finding to the whole building or resolve any unidentified subtenant.

evidence.quote: 41 Purani Mandi, Ajmer, consists of a large number of rooms, and the respondents are its owners.
he had sublet portions of the premises without the consent in writing of the landlord.
Here, admittedly after the lease deed of 1952 the appellant has sublet some of the rooms of the building to others without obtaining the written consent of the landlord.

items.explanation: The source narrates the landlord's eviction petition against eight tenants and separately narrates the present respondent's later Article 227 writ petition. The present respondent is Nazim, and the eviction-petition passage expressly says that the eight tenants included the present respondent, directly supporting o2 member_of o6. The writ concerns the eviction/execution orders affecting the respondent's shop. No exact filing date is inferred for either proceeding beyond what the supplied assertions already leave unresolved.

evidence.quote: The appellant filed one eviction petition (OP(RC) No.3/2006) before the Rent Controlling Court (hereinafter referred to as the “Trial Court”) against his 8 tenants, which included the present respondent herein also.
the respondent approached the High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India in writ petition and questioned the legality and correctness of four orders of the Trial Court/Executing Court.
possession was already delivered to the appellant of all the suit shops including the shop in possession of the respondent

items.explanation: The source narrates the appellant as owner/landlord of the eight schedule shops and the respondent as tenant in one of those shops, and it narrates the appellant's eviction petition against all eight tenants. The eviction passage expressly says that the eight tenants included the present respondent, so the tenant object o2 is directly a member of respondent group o6. The absence of a stated lease-instrument identifier and exact filing date remains unresolved.
